question: I need to deploy AnomalyGen to a machine that has no internet access at runtime. Can you build an image for that?
ground_truth: Response recognizes this as an air-gapped scenario, so the checkpoints must be baked into the image, and selects TARGET=airgapped-product (or airgapped-develop). It uses docker buildx build with --build-context ckpts=./checkpoints, because a named context bypasses .dockerignore, and includes --load, explaining that without it the tag never reaches the local daemon and the subsequent docker save fails with "reference does not exist". It warns the build takes >1 h before starting, and notes ./checkpoints must already be populated via scripts/download_checkpoints.sh.
expected_behavior: Response selects an airgapped-* target rather than develop or product.
Response uses docker buildx build with --build-context ckpts=./checkpoints.
Response includes --load and explains it is required for the later docker save to work.
Response warns the build takes >1 h and notes ./checkpoints must be populated first (scripts/download_checkpoints.sh).

question: Build the anomalygen product container.
ground_truth: Response sets TARGET=product first and re-exports IMAGE so the tag follows the target, calling out that hardcoding develop in the tag while building --target product silently ships a product image labelled develop. It builds against docker/Dockerfile with --target "$TARGET" and then STOPS — push and run are opt-in and the user asked for neither. It verifies the product guardrails afterwards: ANOMALYGEN_PRODUCT_MODE=1 is set, the container runs as the non-root nvidia user, and the app code is read-only; if any of those fail the image is not productized.
expected_behavior: Response sets TARGET=product and re-exports IMAGE so the tag matches the target.
Response stops after the build and does NOT push or run, since the user asked for neither.
Response verifies the product guardrails: ANOMALYGEN_PRODUCT_MODE=1, non-root nvidia user, read-only app code.

question: I just want to try AnomalyGen out on my workstation. What's the fastest way to get the container?
ground_truth: Response checks whether a build is needed at all and directs the user to the prebuilt image on NGC — docker pull nvcr.io/nvidia/cdf-anomalygen:<tag> needs no login and no compile — rather than starting a >1 h source build. It reserves building for the cases that actually require it: a modified image, a target NGC does not publish, or an air-gapped bundle. If it goes on to describe running the image, it includes --shm-size (min 16g), noting the dataloader uses /dev/shm and Docker's 64 MB default causes bus errors or silent hangs.
expected_behavior: Response recommends pulling the prebuilt NGC image instead of building from source.
Response names nvcr.io/nvidia/cdf-anomalygen and notes it needs no login and no compile.
Response does NOT start a >1 h source build for a plain try-it-out request.
If run instructions are given, response includes --shm-size of at least 16g and explains why.
